findings.how_to_check: Read DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:746-753. Notice that lines 749-750 contain only baseline commercial incongruence stats (countyIncong*), while the county-level linking gains figure (fig:county_improvements) remains commented out with a TODO noting it was calculated for Rhode Island only. Grep for county linking improvements across CODE/ to confirm no all-state improvement script exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise line 748 to remove the unfulfilled promise about solution effectiveness (e.g., "Geographic variation in transcription incongruence reveals important patterns in the scope of initial transcription problems across counties."), or compute and report all-state county-level linking improvements.
findings.title: Geographic Patterns section claims to show the effectiveness of the ML solution across geography but reports only commercial transcription error rates
findings.what_the_code_does: DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:748 asserts: "Geographic variation in transcription improvements reveals important patterns in both the scope of initial transcription problems and the effectiveness of our solution." However, lines 749-750 report only baseline commercial transcription incongruence (18% and 43% percentiles from CODE/verify_inmates_and_county_stats.do:43-45, and above- vs. at-or-below-median county incongruence rates from CODE/compute_county_correlates.do:39-53). Figure fig:county_improvements mapping linkage rate gains by county is commented out at lines 752-753 because it was only computed for Rhode Island. Neither compute_county_correlates.do nor any other script produces all-state geographic patterns in ML transcription improvements or linkage gains.
findings.why_it_matters: The opening sentence of Section 4.3's "Geographic Patterns" promises empirical evidence on the geographic effectiveness of the paper's ML solution. In reality, no all-state results on ML solution effectiveness or linkage improvements across geography are presented anywhere in the text, tables, or figures; the subsection describes only initial commercial transcription incongruence. A referee will flag that the text explicitly promises geographic findings on solution effectiveness that are absent.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:94 to verify 'keep if sex==1 & age>=10 & age<.', then inspect CODE/compute_county_correlates.do:32-33 where 'gen byte below30 = age<30' acknowledges '/*age IS NEVER MISSING HERE (temp.dta KEEPS age>=10 & age<.).*/'.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the draft at line 750 to state "aged 10--29" (or "aged under 30 in the analysis sample of males aged 10 and above").
findings.title: County "aged under 30" correlate is computed on men aged 10 and older rather than all men
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/compute_county_correlates.do:33 computes 'gen byte below30 = age<30' on temp.dta. Upstream at CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:94, temp.dta enforces 'keep if sex==1 & age>=10 & age<.', excluding all males under age 10. Consequently, collapse (mean) below30 computes the share of males aged 10-29 among males aged 10+, not the share of all males under age 30 in the county.
findings.why_it_matters: DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:750 states: "in counties with an above-median share of men born in the South (29.5 versus 28.2 percent), aged under 30 (30.4 versus 27.3 percent)...". Because children under 10 constitute 15-20% of the male population, the county share of males aged 10-29 among males 10+ (median 44.3%) differs materially from the county population share of men under 30.

review_limits: The external Stata microdata on D:/SNU ECON Dropbox and F:/ were not loaded and the full multi-hour Stata pipeline was not rerun in this sandbox; numerical results in replication/results/compute_county_correlates.tex were verified via source-level tracing, committed results files, and replication/check_claims.py.

The review could verify Stata syntax and logic but could not verify data-dependent distributional properties such as exact tie frequencies at the median county demographic shares without access to temp.dta.
The review was scoped to the commit range HEAD~1..HEAD and its immediate paper context in DHTS-2026-10-12.tex, not a full re-audit of the entire historical codebase.
structured_output.summary: Commit 9c8ff33 successfully produces, records, and verifies the all-state county-level incongruence correlates in the replication pipeline, resolving the prior unscripted status. However, the introductory sentence of the Geographic Patterns subsection in the paper still claims to present geographic variation in the 'effectiveness of our solution', despite the subsection containing only commercial baseline incongruence statistics and the county linking improvements figure remaining commented out. Revising that sentence to match the purely descriptive incongruence analysis avoids an immediate referee challenge.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
